questions.text: Which AWS CLI command would you use to create a new training job in Amazon SageMaker?
questions.explanationHtml: The aws sagemaker create-training-job command is used to initiate a new training job in Amazon SageMaker, specifying the training parameters and resources.

questions.text: You need to automate hyperparameter tuning for a deep learning model on Amazon SageMaker. However, you also want to manually set a few hyperparameters. Which strategy should you adopt?

options.text: Use SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning with conditional hyperparameters
Use random search instead of Bayesian optimization
Use SageMaker Processing to handle hyperparameters

questions.explanationHtml: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning supports setting certain hyperparameters manually while tuning others automatically using Bayesian optimization. This allows for a balanced approach to tuning hyperparameters effectively.

questions.text: Your model deployed on Amazon SageMaker is exhibiting high variance. Which strategy can help reduce overfitting?

options.text: Adding more features to the model

questions.explanationHtml: Dropout regularization is a technique used to prevent overfitting by randomly dropping units from the neural network during training. This helps the model to generalize better on unseen data, reducing variance.

questions.text: You need to deploy a machine learning model in a multi-AZ setup to ensure high availability. Which AWS service feature can help you achieve this?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Endpoint Configurations allow you to deploy machine learning models in multiple Availability Zones (AZs) to ensure high availability and fault tolerance. This setup helps in maintaining service continuity in case of an AZ failure.

questions.text: What is the purpose of using batch normalization in neural networks?

options.text: To apply activation functions to the output
To increase the number of layers
To normalize the output of each layer

questions.explanationHtml: Batch normalization normalizes the output of each layer in a neural network, which helps in stabilizing and accelerating the training process by reducing internal covariate shift.

questions.text: Which service is used for real-time data streaming in AWS?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon Kinesis is a platform for real-time data streaming and analytics. It allows you to collect, process, and analyze data streams in real-time, making it useful for applications that require immediate insights from large volumes of data.

questions.text: You are tasked with creating an anomaly detection model for a manufacturing process. Which Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithm is best suited for this task?
questions.explanationHtml: Random Cut Forest (RCF) is a built-in algorithm in Amazon SageMaker that is specifically designed for anomaly detection. It is well-suited for identifying unusual patterns or outliers in datasets, making it ideal for monitoring manufacturing processes.

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of using Amazon SageMaker Studio Lab over traditional Jupyter Notebooks?

options.text: It supports only Python programming language
It is available only for academic use
It provides a managed, secure environment with free compute resources
It requires no AWS account for access

questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Studio Lab offers a managed, secure environment with free compute resources, making it accessible for data scientists to build and test machine learning models without the need for cloud infrastructure management.

questions.text: How can you securely share a trained machine learning model across multiple AWS accounts without exposing the model data?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Model Registry with cross-account access
Deploy the model in one account and use cross-account IAM roles
Share the Amazon S3 bucket containing the model artifacts
Copy the model artifacts to each account manually

questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry allows you to manage and share models securely across multiple AWS accounts by configuring cross-account access, ensuring that model data is not exposed unnecessarily.

questions.text: How does Amazon SageMaker Pipelines enhance the machine learning workflow?

options.text: By enabling continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) of machine learning models

questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Pipelines supports the automation and orchestration of machine learning workflows, enabling continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) practices for machine learning models.

questions.text: Which feature of Amazon SageMaker allows you to monitor the performance of deployed models and detect anomalies?
questions.explanationHtml: SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors the quality of machine learning models in production and detects data and model drift, helping ensure that models maintain high performance and accuracy over time.

questions.text: Which command allows you to update the settings of an existing endpoint in Amazon SageMaker?
questions.explanationHtml: The aws sagemaker update-endpoint command updates the settings of an existing endpoint in Amazon SageMaker. You need to specify the endpoint name and the new endpoint configuration name using the –endpoint-name and –endpoint-config-name flags.

questions.text: Which AWS service is recommended for large-scale distributed training of deep learning models?
questions.explanationHtml: AWS ParallelCluster is an AWS-supported open-source cluster management tool that makes it easy to deploy and manage high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. It is suitable for large-scale distributed training of deep learning models, providing the necessary infrastructure and management capabilities.

questions.text: Which AWS service was the precursor to AWS Glue, providing data integration and ETL capabilities before AWS Glue‘s introduction?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon Data Pipeline was a precursor to AWS Glue, providing data integration and ETL capabilities before AWS Glue was introduced with enhanced features for data preparation.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of using transfer learning in deep learning?

options.text: It ensures 100% accuracy in all tasks
It eliminates the need for model tuning
It increases the complexity of the model
It reduces the need for a large dataset

questions.explanationHtml: Transfer learning leverages pre-trained models and applies their knowledge to new tasks, reducing the need for large datasets and extensive training, especially when labeled data is limited.

questions.text: How does Amazon SageMaker‘s Model Debugger help during the model training phase?

options.text: By identifying and diagnosing issues in model training

questions.explanationHtml: SageMaker Model Debugger helps identify and diagnose issues during model training, such as data quality problems or improper learning rates, allowing for more effective debugging and model improvement.

questions.text: Which service should you use if you want to perform large-scale data processing tasks such as batch analytics or machine learning data preparation?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce) is designed for large-scale data processing tasks, including batch analytics and machine learning data preparation using distributed computing frameworks like Apache Hadoop and Spark.

questions.text: You need to visualize the feature importance of your trained model to stakeholders. Which AWS service can you use to create interactive visualizations?
questions.explanationHtml:
Amazon QuickSight is the most suitable AWS service for creating interactive visualizations of feature importance for your trained model to stakeholders.

Here’s why:

  • Interactive Dashboards: QuickSight excels at building interactive dashboards with various visualization types (bar charts, pie charts, heatmaps, etc.). This allows stakeholders to easily explore the feature importance data, filter results, and gain deeper insights.
  • Data Connectivity: QuickSight can connect to various data sources, including those within AWS (like S3, Redshift) and external sources. You can import the feature importance data from your model training process into QuickSight.  
  • Collaboration & Sharing: QuickSight facilitates easy sharing of dashboards and insights with stakeholders through secure sharing mechanisms and embedded analytics capabilities.  
  • User-Friendly Interface: The intuitive interface of QuickSight makes it relatively easy for users with varying levels of technical expertise to create and interact with visualizations. 

While other services like SageMaker Clarify can provide feature importance information, QuickSight is specifically designed for creating interactive visualizations and sharing them with a broader audience.

Key Considerations:

  • Data Preparation: Ensure your feature importance data is properly formatted and prepared for ingestion into QuickSight.
  • Visualization Design: Choose appropriate visualization types (e.g., bar charts for top features, heatmaps for feature interactions) to effectively communicate the insights to stakeholders.

By leveraging QuickSight’s capabilities, you can effectively communicate the feature importance of your model to stakeholders in a clear, concise, and engaging manner.

questions.text: Which metric is used to evaluate classification models?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

  • Precision and Recall:
    • Precision and Recall are metrics specifically used for evaluating classification models.
    • Precision measures the accuracy of positive predictions (how many of the predicted positives are actually positive).
    • Recall measures the ability of the model to identify all relevant instances (how many of the actual positives are correctly predicted).
    • These metrics are particularly useful for imbalanced datasets and are commonly used in binary and multi-class classification tasks.

Incorrect

  • Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE):
    • RMSE is a metric used for evaluating regression models, not classification models. It measures the average magnitude of the error between predicted and actual values.
    • It is not suitable for classification tasks where the output is categorical.
  • Mean Absolute Error (MAE):
    • MAE is another metric used for regression models. It calculates the average absolute difference between predicted and actual values.
    • Like RMSE, it is not applicable to classification tasks.
  • Mean Squared Error (MSE):
    • MSE is also a regression metric. It measures the average squared difference between predicted and actual values.
    • It is not used for classification models, as it does not account for categorical outcomes.

questions.text: You need to explain the predictions of a black-box model deployed on Amazon SageMaker. Which tool can assist you with this task?
questions.explanationHtml:
The correct answer is Amazon SageMaker Clarify.

Here’s why:

  • Amazon SageMaker Clarify: This tool is specifically designed to detect potential bias in machine learning models and help explain how these models make predictions. It provides insights into feature importance and helps understand the factors influencing model outputs, which is crucial for explaining black-box models.

Here’s why the other options are not the primary solution:

  • Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth: This service helps you build highly accurate training datasets for machine learning. While essential for model development, it doesn’t directly address model explainability.
  • Amazon SageMaker Studio: This is an integrated development environment (IDE) for machine learning. While you can use it to build and deploy models, it doesn’t offer the specialized explainability features of Clarify.
  • Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler: This tool simplifies the process of data preparation and feature engineering. It helps you clean, transform, and analyze data, but it doesn’t provide model explainability capabilities.

questions.text: How can you efficiently preprocess large-scale text data for a natural language processing (NLP) model using AWS services?

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend for text processing
Use AWS Lambda for real-time processing

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

  • Use AWS Glue for ETL

    • AWS Glue is a serverless, scalable data integration and ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) service. It is designed to efficiently handle large-scale data processing, which is crucial for NLP preprocessing steps like tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, stop word removal, and converting text to numerical features (like TF-IDF or word embeddings). Glue automatically scales its processing cluster to manage the size and complexity of the text data, making it the most appropriate and cost-effective tool for batch-oriented data preparation.

Incorrect

  • Use Amazon Comprehend for text processing

    • Amazon Comprehend is an AWS service that provides pre-trained NLP capabilities (like sentiment analysis, entity recognition, and key phrase extraction). While it processes text, it is used for analyzing text and generating insights, not for performing the low-level data preprocessing/ETL steps (like cleaning, structuring, and feature engineering) required to prepare raw text data for a custom machine learning model.

  • Use Amazon Rekognition

    • Amazon Rekognition is an AWS service dedicated to image and video analysis (computer vision tasks, such as object and facial recognition). It has no function related to processing or preparing text data for an NLP model, making it entirely irrelevant to the question.

  • Use AWS Lambda for real-time processing

    • AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service best suited for running short-duration, event-driven functions or real-time inference. It is not designed or optimized for the batch processing of large-scale datasets required for general NLP preprocessing. Running a lengthy ETL job on petabytes of data via Lambda would be highly inefficient and likely hit execution time limits.

questions.text: To view detailed information about a specific training job, which command should you use?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

  • aws sagemaker describe-training-job –training-job-name

    • The AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) consistently uses the describe- prefix to retrieve detailed configuration and status information about a single, specific resource. In the Amazon SageMaker API, the operation for this function is DescribeTrainingJob, and the corresponding CLI command is aws sagemaker describe-training-job. The required parameter to specify which job to view is correctly named --training-job-name.

Incorrect

  • aws sagemaker show-training-job –job-name

    • The CLI does not use the show- prefix for retrieving detailed resource information; this is a non-standard AWS CLI naming convention. While --job-name is a common parameter style, the primary command is incorrect.

  • aws sagemaker get-training-job –name

    • The CLI sometimes uses the get- prefix (e.g., get-caller-identity), but for retrieving the status and configuration details of a specific resource instance like a SageMaker job, the describe- convention is standard and preferred over get-. Also, the parameter name --name is too generic for this command’s required input.

  • aws sagemaker describe-job –name

    • This command is incorrect because it is too broad and doesn’t specify the resource type within SageMaker. AWS services often have multiple job types (e.g., training jobs, processing jobs, transform jobs). The command must include the resource type, making describe-training-job the correct format. Additionally, --name is usually not the specific parameter name required by this API call.

questions.text: When dealing with time-series data, which Amazon SageMaker feature would you use to ensure the data is correctly partitioned and aligned?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

  • SageMaker Data Wrangler

    • SageMaker Data Wrangler is a feature designed to accelerate the process of data aggregation and preparation (ETL) for machine learning. It offers a visual interface and built-in transformations to quickly clean, normalize, and feature-engineer data. For time-series data, Data Wrangler has specific capabilities to handle common challenges, including:

      • Time-Series Alignment: Ensuring data points are correctly synchronized across different series.

      • Partitioning: Structuring the data based on time or other keys (e.g., product ID, location) to optimize training and retrieval, which is crucial for large-scale time-series datasets.

    • This tool provides the features necessary to ensure the time-series data is ready for a forecasting model.

Incorrect

  • SageMaker Ground Truth

    • SageMaker Ground Truth is a service used to label datasets for machine learning (e.g., drawing bounding boxes on images or classifying text). It has no function for data partitioning, alignment, or general feature engineering of time-series data.

  • SageMaker Time Series Forecasting

    • While this service refers to the overall task, SageMaker Time Series Forecasting (which uses the built-in DeepAR algorithm or the Forecast component of SageMaker Canvas) is the modeling and inference step, not the data preparation or feature engineering step. Data must be correctly partitioned and aligned before it is fed into this forecasting service.

  • SageMaker Processing

    • SageMaker Processing provides a highly scalable and cost-effective method to run custom data processing workloads (like Spark, scikit-learn, or custom code) for ML preparation. While you could write code within a Processing job to partition and align time-series data, Data Wrangler (Option A) is the purpose-built, higher-level, and more efficient feature that simplifies and accelerates these specific, common preparation tasks without requiring you to write custom code. Therefore, Data Wrangler is the better and more direct answer.

questions.text: Which machine learning algorithm is most suitable for binary classification tasks?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

  • Logistic Regression

    • Logistic Regression is a classification algorithm used to estimate the probability of a discrete outcome given an input variable. It uses a sigmoid function to map predicted values to a probability between 0 and 1. This probability is then interpreted to classify the input into one of two categories (e.g., Yes/No, 0/1, Spam/Not Spam), making it the most suitable and efficient choice for a fundamental binary classification task.

Incorrect

  • Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

    • PCA is a dimensionality reduction technique, not a classification algorithm.4 Its primary purpose is to transform a large set of variables into a smaller one that still contains most of the information, typically used as a preprocessing step before training a machine learning model.5 It cannot be used directly to perform classification.

  • K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)

    • K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) is a non-parametric classification algorithm that can be used for binary classification.6 However, compared to Logistic Regression, KNN is computationally expensive during the prediction phase (as it must calculate distances to all training data points) and is sensitive to the scale and dimensionality of the data.7 Logistic Regression is the simpler, more foundational, and most efficient model specifically designed for the output of a binary outcome, making it the best answer in an AIF-C01 context.

  • K-Means

    • K-Means is an unsupervised clustering algorithm.8 Its purpose is to group similar data points together into $K$ clusters without using pre-labeled data. It is used for tasks like segmentation, not for the supervised learning task of classification (predicting a label based on historical labels).

questions.text: Which command allows you to start a hyperparameter tuning job in Amazon SageMaker?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

aws sagemaker create-hyperparameter-tuning-job

  • Correct because the AWS CLI command to initiate a hyperparameter tuning job in SageMaker is create-hyperparameter-tuning-job.
  • This command creates a new tuning job, specifying the training job definition, ranges of hyperparameters, and objective metrics.
  • The keyword is “create”, not “start,” because SageMaker jobs are created and then executed automatically once defined.

Incorrect

aws sagemaker start-hyperparameter-tuning-job

  • Incorrect because there is no “start-hyperparameter-tuning-job” command in the AWS CLI.
  • The correct verb is “create”, not “start.”

aws sagemaker create-tuning-job

  • Incorrect because the command must explicitly reference hyperparameter tuning jobs.
  • “create-tuning-job” is not a valid SageMaker CLI command.

aws sagemaker start-tuning-job

  • Incorrect because, similar to Option A, there is no “start-tuning-job” command.
  • Again, the correct verb is “create”, and the full command must include hyperparameter-tuning-job.

questions.text: Which command would you use to delete a SageMaker endpoint configuration?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

aws sagemaker delete-endpoint-configuration --endpoint-config-name <config_name>

  • Correct because the AWS CLI command to delete a SageMaker endpoint configuration is delete-endpoint-configuration.
  • The required parameter is --endpoint-config-name, which specifies the name of the endpoint configuration to be deleted.
  • This is the official syntax supported by the AWS CLI.

Incorrect

aws sagemaker delete-config --endpoint-name <config_name>

  • Incorrect because there is no delete-config command in SageMaker CLI.
  • Also, the parameter --endpoint-name refers to an endpoint, not an endpoint configuration.

aws sagemaker remove-endpoint-config --name <config_name>

  • Incorrect because remove-endpoint-config is not a valid SageMaker CLI command.
  • AWS CLI uses delete-endpoint-configuration, not remove.

aws sagemaker delete-endpoint-config --name <config_name>

  • Incorrect because while it looks close, the correct command is delete-endpoint-configuration.
  • The parameter must be --endpoint-config-name, not --name.

questions.text: To view the logs for a SageMaker training job, which AWS CLI command should you use?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

aws logs get-log-events

  • Correct because SageMaker training job logs are stored in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
  • To view them, you use the CloudWatch Logs CLI command aws logs get-log-events, specifying the log group and stream associated with the training job.
  • This retrieves the actual log events generated during training.

Incorrect

aws sagemaker get-training-job-logs

  • Incorrect because there is no such CLI command in SageMaker. Logs are not retrieved directly from SageMaker but from CloudWatch.

aws sagemaker describe-training-job

  • Incorrect because this command provides metadata about the training job (status, hyperparameters, resource configuration), but it does not return logs.

aws logs describe-log-groups

  • Incorrect because this command lists available log groups in CloudWatch. It does not retrieve the actual log events for a training job.

questions.text: What is the primary use of AWS DeepLens?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Edge computing for machine learning

  • Correct because AWS DeepLens is a deep learning–enabled video camera designed for edge computing.
  • It allows developers to run machine learning models locally on the device, enabling real‑time computer vision tasks such as object detection, facial recognition, and activity recognition without needing to send all data to the cloud.
  • This reduces latency, improves performance, and supports scenarios where connectivity is limited.

Incorrect

Data pipeline management

  • Incorrect because data pipeline management is handled by services like AWS Data Pipeline or AWS Glue, not DeepLens.
  • DeepLens is focused on edge ML inference, not orchestrating or managing data pipelines.

Real‑time data analytics

  • Incorrect because real‑time analytics is better achieved with services like Amazon Kinesis or Amazon Redshift.
  • While DeepLens can process video streams locally, its purpose is ML inference at the edge, not full analytics pipelines.

Storage of large datasets

  • Incorrect because DeepLens is not a storage solution.
  • Large dataset storage is handled by Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS, whereas DeepLens is a device for running ML models, not storing bulk data.

questions.text: What is “cross-validation“ used for in machine learning?

options.text: To evaluate the performance of a model on different subsets of the data
To ensure the model uses the correct algorithms
To increase the size of the dataset
To combine multiple models into a single prediction

questions.explanationHtml: Cross-validation is a technique used to assess how well a model performs on different subsets of the data, ensuring that the model generalizes well and is not overfitting.

questions.text: Which method can be used to optimize hyperparameters in Amazon SageMaker?
questions.explanationHtml: Hyperparameter optimization in Amazon SageMaker can be performed using various methods, including manual tuning, grid search, and Bayesian optimization. Each method has its own advantages and can be chosen based on the specific requirements of the machine learning task.

questions.text: Which of the following AWS services is used to analyze large datasets with high speed?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce) is a cloud big data platform for processing vast amounts of data using open-source tools such as Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark. It enables fast processing of large datasets and is commonly used for data analysis, machine learning, and data transformation.

questions.text: Which of the following describes the concept of model drift in the context of machine learning?

options.text: Gradual improvement in model performance over time
Expansion of model capabilities to new tasks
Degradation of model performance due to changes in data patterns
Significant increase in model accuracy after retraining

questions.explanationHtml: Model drift occurs when the statistical properties of the input data change over time, leading to a degradation in model performance. Monitoring for model drift is crucial for maintaining the accuracy and reliability of machine learning models.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key feature of supervised learning?

options.text: The model learns without labeled data
The model is trained using input-output pairs
The model learns to group data into clusters

questions.explanationHtml: Supervised learning involves training a model using labeled data, where the input data is paired with the correct output. The model learns to predict the output from the input data based on this training.

questions.text: Which AWS service would you use to securely manage and store access keys for your machine learning application?
questions.explanationHtml: AWS Secrets Manager is a service designed to securely store and manage sensitive information such as access keys, passwords, and API keys. It helps in securely accessing these credentials within your machine learning application without hardcoding them into your code.

questions.text: Which type of neural network is best suited for processing sequential data in natural language processing tasks?
questions.explanationHtml: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are designed to handle sequential data and time-series information, making them well-suited for natural language processing tasks such as language modeling, text generation, and translation.

questions.text: How does Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor help in maintaining the quality of deployed models?

options.text: By detecting data and model quality issues in real-time

questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors the data being processed by deployed models and can detect issues such as data drift, model bias, and prediction errors in real-time. This helps maintain the quality and reliability of machine learning models in production.

questions.text: Which AWS service can be used to create personalized recommendations for users?
questions.explanationHtml: AWS Personalize is a machine learning service that allows developers to create individualized recommendations for customers using their applications. It can be used to build recommendation engines similar to those used by Amazon.com.

questions.text: Which command would you use to create an endpoint configuration in Amazon SageMaker?
questions.explanationHtml: The aws sagemaker create-endpoint-config command creates a new endpoint configuration in Amazon SageMaker. You need to specify the endpoint configuration name and the production variants using the –endpoint-config-name and –production-variants flags.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of using Amazon SageMaker Neo for model optimization?

options.text: It offers built-in data visualization tools
It reduces the size and increases the speed of machine learning models
It integrates with AWS CodePipeline for continuous deployment
It provides an automatic data cleaning feature

questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Neo optimizes machine learning models to run faster and more efficiently on multiple hardware platforms, including cloud instances and edge devices, by reducing their size and improving their inference speed.

questions.text: Which of the following strategies is most effective for managing data drift in machine learning models on AWS?

options.text: Retraining models periodically with Amazon SageMaker

questions.explanationHtml: To manage data drift, it is essential to periodically retrain machine learning models with updated data. Amazon SageMaker provides capabilities for automating the retraining process, ensuring that models remain accurate and perform well over time as data distributions change.

questions.text: Which AWS service allows you to create and train machine learning models without having to set up and manage the underlying infrastructure?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker is a fully managed service that provides all the necessary tools to build, train, and deploy machine learning models without the need for managing the underlying infrastructure, making it easier for developers and data scientists to focus on their models.

questions.text: Your model‘s performance has degraded over time due to changes in the data distribution. Which AWS service can help you detect these changes automatically?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors the data flowing to the deployed models and can detect changes in data distribution, known as data drift. It helps in maintaining model performance by alerting you to potential issues.

questions.text: How can you monitor the status of a batch transform job in Amazon SageMaker?
questions.explanationHtml: The aws sagemaker describe-transform-job command provides detailed information about a batch transform job, including its status. You need to specify the name of the transform job using the –transform-job-name flag.

questions.text: You need to deploy a machine learning model for real-time predictions and ensure low latency. Which AWS service is best suited for this task?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Endpoints provide a way to deploy machine learning models for real-time predictions with low latency. They are scalable and can handle a large volume of requests, making them suitable for applications that require quick responses.

questions.text: Which strategy can help you improve the scalability and efficiency of batch inference jobs on large datasets in Amazon SageMaker?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Batch Transform with distributed data loading

questions.explanationHtml: Using Amazon SageMaker Batch Transform with distributed data loading improves the scalability and efficiency of batch inference jobs by distributing the data across multiple instances, allowing for parallel processing of large datasets.

questions.text: What is the primary function of AWS IoT Core?
questions.explanationHtml: AWS IoT Core is a managed cloud service that allows connected devices to interact with cloud applications and other devices. It provides secure, bi-directional communication between IoT devices and the AWS cloud, enabling device management and data collection.

questions.text: You are using Amazon SageMaker to train a neural network. Despite having a large dataset, your model is overfitting. Which combination of techniques can help mitigate this issue?

options.text: Increase the learning rate and reduce the number of layers
Use data augmentation and early stopping
Decrease the learning rate and increase the number of epochs
Apply dropout and use a larger batch size

questions.explanationHtml: Data augmentation increases the diversity of the training data without actually collecting new data, helping to prevent overfitting. Early stopping helps in halting the training process before the model starts overfitting the training data.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of AWS Comprehend?
questions.explanationHtml: AWS Comprehend is a natural language processing (NLP) service that uses machine learning to find insights and relationships in text. It helps to analyze text documents and extract key phrases, sentiments, entities, and language.

questions.text: Your model deployed on Amazon SageMaker is returning inconsistent results. Which combination of tools can help you diagnose and resolve the issue?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon SageMaker Debugger
AWS CloudTrail and Amazon SageMaker Studio

questions.explanationHtml: Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon SageMaker Debugger can be used together to monitor model performance and diagnose issues. CloudWatch provides logging and monitoring, while SageMaker Debugger offers real-time debugging and analysis of training jobs.

questions.text: How do you list all the models in your SageMaker account using the AWS CLI?
questions.explanationHtml: The aws sagemaker list-models command lists all the models in your SageMaker account. This command provides a summary of each model, including the model name and creation time.

questions.text: You need to stop a running training job in Amazon SageMaker. Which command should you use?
questions.explanationHtml: The aws sagemaker stop-training-job command stops a running training job in Amazon SageMaker. You need to specify the name of the training job to stop using the –training-job-name flag.

questions.text: Which AWS service can be used to create automated data labeling workflows that include human labeling?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth provides capabilities for creating automated data labeling workflows that include both machine learning and human labeling. It integrates with Amazon Mechanical Turk and other workforce providers to deliver high-quality labeled data.

questions.text: What does AWS Glue primarily provide?
questions.explanationHtml: AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service that makes it easy to prepare and integrate data for analytics, machine learning, and application development. It provides data integration capabilities to move and transform data from various sources.

questions.text: Which recent AWS service provides serverless inference for machine learning models?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference is a recent service that provides a serverless infrastructure for hosting machine learning models, allowing users to deploy models without managing the underlying infrastructure.

questions.text: Your team needs to label a large amount of data for a computer vision project. Which AWS service provides an efficient solution for this task, including active learning capabilities?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth provides a scalable solution for labeling data, including features like active learning to reduce the amount of data that needs to be manually labeled. It integrates with human labeling services to ensure high-quality annotations for training models.

questions.text: Which AWS service can be used to transcribe audio files into text?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon Transcribe is an automatic speech recognition (ASR) service that allows developers to add speech-to-text capabilities to their applications. It is used to convert audio files into text, making it easier to analyze and process spoken content.
